chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“The slightest form of shirk is that a man innovates an opinion, then loves on its basis and hates on its basis.”

key_terms.الشِّرْكِ: shirk; associating partners with Allah, here indicating a subtle form of deviation
key_terms.فَيُحِبَّ: then he loves based upon it
key_terms.يَبْتَدِعَ: to innovate or invent without divine basis

ai.seo_question: What is the lowest or slightest form of shirk according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that even a subtle form of shirk can appear when a person invents a viewpoint and makes it the basis of loyalty and enmity. It condemns centering love and hate on self-made opinion rather than truth grounded in divine guidance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4955 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
"The slightest form of polytheism is when a man invents an opinion and then loves and hates based on it."
